description: Diffs never leave the customer's network during enforcement. Hook payloads and session diffs stay local; only license validation and capture classification traverse to Drift Cloud.
Phase 1 warning hooks must return in under 150ms p95. Semantic evaluation and LLM round-trips belong in Phase 2 (Stop hook), never inline during coding.
Semantic evaluation has a configurable per-session max LLM call count. When exhausted, unchecked rules are logged and the engine proceeds — never silently retry or expand budget.
Config schema is versioned and forward-compatible across minor versions. Breaking changes require a major bump and migration tooling.

When license is invalid, expired, or unreachable, the container must NOT hard-brick. OSS-equivalent rule engine and hook endpoint keep running with user-authored config. Paid features gate off with a clear error.
Override directives must carry a rule name and a non-empty reason. Per-rule policies may additionally require a linked ticket or disallow overrides entirely.
After the initial attach, KG builds are incremental — only changed files are re-parsed. Full rebuild is an explicit operator action, not an automatic behavior.
Never use __dirname or hardcoded absolute paths to reference repo-root files. Use process.cwd() plus environment overrides for runtime path resolution.
Wire pipelines end-to-end. Do not leave zero-vector placeholders or stub implementations silently. If something is not yet implemented, flag it explicitly.
